To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fungi that bioconvert the energy grasses Miscanthus and/or sugarcane are superior to Trichoderma on all counts, and the best are in taxonomic orders that have never been used for industrial bioconversion.

we isolated and characterized 30 fungi, all of which were isolated from decays of energy grasses, and all of which were able to bioconvert Miscanthis cell walls, secrete enzymes, and remove plant cell wall components.

fungi from decaying energy crops are better than the best industrial bioconversion fungi at bioconverting energy crops, secreting enzymes, secreting enzymes with specific activities, and removing specific parts of the plant cell walls of energy crops.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new, superior bioconversion fungi and the enzymes they secrete, and with the discovery of fungi that can remove specific components of plant cell walls.
identifying the fungi best suited for bioconversion of the energy grasses Miscanthus and/or sugarcane, and we believe we have found some of them.

identifying the most effective fungi to use for bioconversion of plant biomass and to use as sources of plant cell wall enzymes for biofuel production, and we have found fungi that are significantly more effective than Trichoderma for these purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have identified fungi that bioconvert Miscanthum and sugarcane, that secrete large amounts of protein and enzymes, and that remove significant portions of the cell wall.
fungi from decaying energy crops are superior to T. reesei for the bioconversion of Miscanthus to ethanol.
the fungi we have studied are superior to T. reesei and that they are worthy of further study as bioconversion fungi for energy crops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fungi that naturally bioconvert energy crop cell walls can be used for industrial bioconversion.
fungi isolated from energy grasses are superior to Trichoderma for biomass conversion, enzyme production, and plant cell wall deconstructions.

we have discovered fungi that are superior to T. reesei in all of the following: biomass conversion; total protein secretion; enzyme activity; removal of plant cell walls; and ability to grow on a medium containing only Miscanthus cell wall.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best bioconversion fungi for energy grasses may come from those that are found in nature on the plants that we want to bioconvert.
fungi isolated from the plants that we want to bioconvert are the best fungi to use in bioconversion.
fungi from the environment that are not yet used for bioconversion are likely to provide better enzymes for bioconversion than fungi that are already in use.
